samples.answer: A token is a small unit of text—typically a word, part of a word, or punctuation—that language models break text into before processing it. Tokens are the basic vocabulary pieces the model reads and generates, since models work with these discrete units rather than raw characters. For example, "unbelievable" might be split into tokens like "un," "believ," and "able," and common short words like "the" usually count as single tokens.
